mapping_rules.no_equivalent: A null platform value means no mapped source field; never interpret as unsupported or supported without a separate qualified API capability observation.
mapping_rules.no_auto_security: Required firewall, isolation and traffic policy remains critical regardless of field presence or a nominal transformation.
mapping_rules.no_copy_native_ids: VM, disk, network, project, controller, host and storage identifiers are installation-local and must be remapped.
mapping_rules.freshness: Use minimum age of needed contributing observations; revalidate all critical source, target, owner and API-version evidence at native effect.

fields.semantic_constraints: Identifiers are source-local, never reused at target.
OpenStack created timestamp is weaker evidence than VMware instance UUID or AHV generation UUID.
No OpenStack BIOS UUID in the source manifest; never synthesize.
Projects are environment-scoped and cannot be copied.
OpenStack tenant APIs may not expose host identity.
Platform release names are not comparable; version-bind per installed service.
OpenStack microversions and AHV namespaces evolve independently.
vSphere revision and Prism update timestamp have distinct meanings.
OFF/poweredOff/SHUTOFF normalization needs explicit transitional-state rejection.
AHV sockets × cores/socket × threads/core; preserve hardware topology separately.
AHV byte count must divide exactly by 1048576; no silent rounding.
OpenStack image metadata/VMware guestId are declarations, not running OS proof.
Map BIOS/UEFI; OpenStack metadata is unverified without guest evidence.
Missing OpenStack secure boot source field means unknown, not disabled.
Virtual TPM is key-bearing: preserve state only through qualified support.
Tools and guest agents are vendor-specific; cannot be directly transplanted.
Nova attachment list omits image-backed local root and ephemeral disks.
Native disk keys/volume IDs are never portable.
Cinder/Flavor sizes are GiB; retain separate root/volume device identities.
SCSI/NVMe controller key, AHV bus/index, and Nova root name differ.
Backings and snapshot chains do not map one-to-one.
Shared/external disks and multiattach require fencing and special methods.
Boolean or key ID does not establish exportable encryption keys.

api_fields: POST images + task status + source disk readback

fields.semantic_constraints: Per-platform export and snapshot operations have different scopes.
OpenStack ports must have complete paging and tenant ownership.
Neutron binding:vnic_type is not the virtual guest hardware model.
MAC continuity requires authorization and collision detection.
Admin state and native attachment states have different semantics.
No direct portgroup/VPC/network UUID translation.
Neutron security-group metadata is not a portable firewall policy.
PCI/GPU passthrough requires explicit support or migration is blocked.
A label is never a stable VM ID.
Creation time does not imply VM incarnation identity.
Capabilities must be negotiated per API family; never require matching cross-vendor version.
Resource pool/cluster/AZ/flavor do not have identical placement semantics.
Measured compute usage and a separate owner reservation are required.
Datastore/container/volume type availability is not per-VM free capacity.
Nutanix maxCapacityBytes is maximum, not allocatable free capacity; never infer availability.
VLANs, subnets, VPCs and routes must be mapped by owner intent.
Security groups, NSX/vSphere and microseg policies need independent allow/deny evidence.
Required firewall/isolation policies are never optional.
Firmware and boot drivers must be tested on destination.

api_fields: POST images + task.status + image URL readback

fields.semantic_constraints: Prism image import vs Glance direct import differ; VMware OVF includes import/provision.
vSphere ImportVApp vs Prism/Nova create need separate qualification.
Roles, project scope, licensing and quotas require installed-time owner evidence.
VMware tags and Nutanix categories can differ in policy semantics; never silently omit functional labels.
